# Task

## Task Description

aggregate and summarize Malaysian airport arrival data, including flight counts and calculate the distances between Malaysian airports in kilometers.

## Environment

You are working with a dbt (data build tool) project that transforms data in a DuckDB database. The project is located in `/workspace` with the following structure:

- `dbt_project.yml` - dbt project configuration
- `profiles.yml` - Database connection profile (DuckDB)
- `models/` - SQL transformation models
- `*.duckdb` - Source database containing raw data

## Objective

Complete or fix the dbt models to produce the correct table outputs. Run `dbt run` to execute the transformations.

## Execution Requirements

- Working directory: `/workspace`
- Run `dbt deps` first if there's a `packages.yml` file (to install dependencies)
- Run `dbt run` to execute all models
- The database file (`*.duckdb`) contains both source data and will store your model outputs
- You can inspect tables using: `duckdb <database>.duckdb -c "SELECT * FROM table_name LIMIT 10;"`

You should solve the task in 30 minutes. You can access 1 CPU, 2 GB memory, 10 GB storage. Do not cheat by using online solutions or hints specific to this task.

file.content:
version: 2


models:
  - name: base_airports
    description: |
      The cleaned version of `raw_airports`.

      _Note: The default materialisation of this table is `ephemeral`,
      but it is overridden in the SQL to be materialised as a `table` instead.
      This is so that indexes can be assigned._

    columns:
      - name: airport_id
        description: "Unique OpenFlights identifier for this airport."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: name
        description: "Name of airport. May or may not contain the City name."
      
      - name: city
        description: "Main city served by airport. May be spelled differently from Name."

      - name: country
        description: >
          Country or territory where airport is located.
          See [Countries](https://openflights.org/data.html#country) to cross-reference to ISO 3166-1 codes.

      - name: iata
        description: "3-letter IATA code. `Null` if not assigned/unknown."

      - name: icao
        description: "4-letter ICAO code. `Null` if not assigned."

      - name: latitude
        description: "Decimal degrees, usually to six significant digits. Negative is South, positive is North."

      - name: longitude
        description: "Decimal degrees, usually to six significant digits. Negative is West, positive is East."

      - name: altitude
        description: "In feet."

      - name: timezone
        description: |
          Hours offset from UTC.

          Fractional hours are expressed as decimals, eg. India is 5.5.

      - name: dst
        description: |
          Daylight savings time.

          One of E (Europe), A (US/Canada), S (South America),
          O (Australia), Z (New Zealand), N (None) or U (Unknown).

          See also: [Help: Time](https://openflights.org/help/time.html)

      - name: database_time_zone
        description: >
          Timezone in ["tz" (Olson) format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database),
          eg. "America/Los_Angeles".

      - name: type
        description: |
          Type of the airport.

          Value "airport" for air terminals, "station" for train stations,
          "port" for ferry terminals and "unknown" if not known.

          In this table, only type=airport is included.

      - name: source
        description: |
          Source of this data.

          "OurAirports" for data sourced from [OurAirports](http://ourairports.com/data/),
          "Legacy" for old data not matched to OurAirports (mostly DAFIF),
          "User" for unverified user contributions.

          In this table, only source=OurAirports is included.



  - name: base_arrivals__malaysia
    description: |
      The cleaned version of `raw_arrivals`.

      Transformation made were:
      - Named table to reflect that data only has Malaysian airports.
      - Renaming of columns to be more descriptive.
      - Casting strings columns to proper Postgres type.
      - Add additional column(s) for more context.

      _Note: The default materialisation of this table is `ephemeral`,
      but it is overridden in the SQL to be materialised as a `table` instead.
      This is so that indexes can be assigned._

    columns:
      - name: sort_time_utc
        description: "The timestamp (UTC) that FlightStats uses to sort flights in their system."

      - name: arrival_timestamp
        description: "The timestamp (MYT) of the expected flight arrival _(i.e. `sort_time_utc + 8 hours` )_."

      - name: operated_by
        description: "A description of the flight operator and on behalf of other airlines, if any."

      - name: full_url
        description: "The full URL users can open and be directed to the respective flight status page."
        tests:
          - not_null
          - unique

      - name: arrival_date
        description: "The arrival date."

      - name: arrival_iata
        description: "3-letter IATA code for the arrival airport."

      - name: arrival_icao
        description: "4-letter ICAO code for the arrival airport."

      - name: arrival_airport_name
        description: "The name of the arrival (destination) airport."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: departure_time_time_am_pm
        description: >
          The published departure time (local to the airport) for the flight
          provided by the airline's operating schedule in AM/PM.

      - name: departure_time_time_24
        description: >
          The published departure time (local to the airport) for the flight
          provided by the airline's operating schedule in 24-hour military time.

      - name: arrival_time_time_am_pm
        description: >
          The published arrival time (local to the airport) for the flight
          provided by the airline's operating schedule in AM/PM.

      - name: arrival_time_time_24
        description: >
          The published arrival time (local to the airport) for the flight
          provided by the airline's operating schedule in 24-hour military time.

      - name: carrier_fs
        description: "The Cirium code for the carrier, globally unique across time."

      - name: carrier_name
        description: "The name of the carrier."

      - name: carrier_flight_number
        description: "The flight identification number and any additional characters."

      - name: departure_airport_fs
        description: "The Cirium code for the departure airport, globally unique across time."

      - name: departure_airport_city
        description: "The city with which the departure airport is associated."

      - name: is_code_share
        description: >
          Boolean value indicating if the marketed flight is a
          [codeshare](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Codeshare_agreement)
        tests:
          - accepted_values:
              values:
                - "true"
                - "false"

models:
  - name: base_airports
    description: |
      The cleaned version of `raw_airports`.

      _Note: The default materialisation of this table is `ephemeral`,
      but it is overridden in the SQL to be materialised as a `table` instead.
      This is so that indexes can be assigned._

    columns:
      - name: airport_id
        description: "Unique OpenFlights identifier for this airport."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: name
        description: "Name of airport. May or may not contain the City name."
      
      - name: city
        description: "Main city served by airport. May be spelled differently from Name."

      - name: country
        description: >
          Country or territory where airport is located.
          See [Countries](https://openflights.org/data.html#country) to cross-reference to ISO 3166-1 codes.

      - name: iata
        description: "3-letter IATA code. `Null` if not assigned/unknown."

      - name: icao
        description: "4-letter ICAO code. `Null` if not assigned."

      - name: latitude
        description: "Decimal degrees, usually to six significant digits. Negative is South, positive is North."

      - name: longitude
        description: "Decimal degrees, usually to six significant digits. Negative is West, positive is East."

      - name: altitude
        description: "In feet."

      - name: timezone
        description: |
          Hours offset from UTC.

          Fractional hours are expressed as decimals, eg. India is 5.5.

      - name: dst
        description: |
          Daylight savings time.

          One of E (Europe), A (US/Canada), S (South America),
          O (Australia), Z (New Zealand), N (None) or U (Unknown).

          See also: [Help: Time](https://openflights.org/help/time.html)

      - name: database_time_zone
        description: >
          Timezone in ["tz" (Olson) format](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tz_database),
          eg. "America/Los_Angeles".

        description: |
          Type of the airport.

          Value "airport" for air terminals, "station" for train stations,
          "port" for ferry terminals and "unknown" if not known.

          In this table, only type=airport is included.

          "OurAirports" for data sourced from [OurAirports](http://ourairports.com/data/),

          "User" for unverified user contributions.

with base_airports as (

    select * from {{ ref('base_airports') }}

),

base_dist as (

    select
        a."name"                                    as a_name,
        b."name"                                    as b_name,
        a.latitude                                  as a_lat,
        a.longitude                                 as a_lon,
        b.latitude                                  as b_lat,
        b.longitude                                 as b_lon,
        (b.latitude - a.latitude) * pi() / 180      as lat_dist,
        (b.longitude - a.longitude) * pi() / 180    as lon_dist

    from
        base_airports a

        cross join
            base_airports b

    where
        a.country = 'Malaysia'
    and
        b.country = 'Malaysia'

    order by
        1,
        2

),

base_area as (

    select
        *,

            + ((a_lat) * pi() / 180)
                * ((b_lat) * pi() / 180)

                        * sin(lon_dist / 2)     as area

    from
        base_dist

),

distance as (

    select
        a_name,
        replace(b_name, ' ', '_') as b_name,
        6371 * 2 * atan2(sqrt(area), sqrt(1-area) ) as distance_km

    from
        base_area

    order by
        1,
        2

)

select * from distance

29	
30	    order by
31	        1,
32	        2
33	
34	),
35	
36	base_area as (
37	
38	    select
39	        *,
40	        sin(lat_dist / 2) * sin(lat_dist / 2)
41	            + ((a_lat) * pi() / 180)
42	                * ((b_lat) * pi() / 180)
43	                    * sin(lon_dist / 2)
44	                        * sin(lon_dist / 2)     as area
45	
46	    from
47	        base_dist
48	
49	),
50	
51	distance as (
52	
53	    select
54	        a_name,
55	        replace(b_name, ' ', '_') as b_name,
56	        6371 * 2 * atan2(sqrt(area), sqrt(1-area) ) as distance_km
57	
58	    from
59	        base_area
60	
61	    order by
62	        1,
63	        2
64	
65	)
66	
67	select * from distance

  - name: fct_arrivals__malaysia_summary
    description: >
      This model provides a summary of flight arrivals to Malaysian airports, including information on the airport's name, location, and the number of arriving flights for the most recent available date. 
      The data is filtered to include only non-code-shared flights.

    refs:
      - name: base_airports

    columns:
      - name: airport_id
        description: "Unique OpenFlights identifier for each airport."

          - not_null

      - name: longitude
        description: "Longitude of the airport in decimal degrees. Negative is West, positive is East."

version: 2

models:
  - name: fct_arrivals__malaysia_summary
    description: >
      This model provides a summary of flight arrivals to Malaysian airports, including information on the airport's name, location, and the number of arriving flights for the most recent available date. 
      The data is filtered to include only non-code-shared flights.

    refs:
      - name: base_airports
      - name: base_arrivals__malaysia

    columns:
      - name: airport_id
        description: "Unique OpenFlights identifier for each airport."
        tests:
          - unique
          - not_null

      - name: name
        description: "Name of the airport. May or may not contain the city name."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: latitude
        description: "Latitude of the airport in decimal degrees. Negative is South, positive is North."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: longitude
        description: "Longitude of the airport in decimal degrees. Negative is West, positive is East."
        tests:
          - not_null

      - name: flight_count
        description: >
          The total number of flight arrivals to each airport on the most recent available date, excluding code-share flights.
        tests:
          - not_null

  - name: fct_airports__malaysia_distances_km

python3 -c "
import duckdb
print('DuckDB version:', duckdb.__version__)
con = duckdb.connect()
# Test PIVOT syntax
try:
    result = con.execute('''
        CREATE TABLE test_pivot AS 
        SELECT 'a' as grp, 'x' as col, 1 as val
        UNION ALL SELECT 'a', 'y', 2
        UNION ALL SELECT 'b', 'x', 3
        UNION ALL SELECT 'b', 'y', 4
    ''')
    print('Test table created')
    
    # Try DuckDB pivot syntax
    result = con.execute('''
        PIVOT test_pivot ON col USING max(val) GROUP BY grp
    ''').fetchdf()
    print('PIVOT result:')
    print(result)
except Exception as e:
    print(f'Error with PIVOT ON USING: {e}')
    
    # Try alternative syntax
    try:
        result = con.execute('''
            FROM test_pivot
            PIVOT (max(val) FOR col IN ('x', 'y'))
            GROUP BY grp
        ''').fetchdf()
        print('FROM PIVOT result:')
        print(result)
    except Exception as e2:
        print(f'Error with FROM PIVOT: {e2}')
print()
print('atan2 test:', con.execute('SELECT atan2(1, 1)').fetchone())
"

python3 -c "
import duckdb
con = duckdb.connect('/workspace/airport.duckdb')

# Check Malaysian airports
print('=== Malaysian airports ===')
result = con.execute(\"SELECT airport_id, name, city, iata, latitude, longitude FROM raw_airports WHERE country = 'Malaysia'\").fetchdf()
print(result.to_string())
print()

# Check arrival dates
print('=== Distinct arrival dates ===')
result = con.execute(\"SELECT DISTINCT date FROM raw_arrivals ORDER BY date\").fetchdf()
print(result.to_string())
print()

# Check isCodeshare values  
print('=== isCodeshare distribution ===')
result = con.execute('SELECT isCodeshare, COUNT(*) as cnt FROM raw_arrivals GROUP BY isCodeshare').fetchdf()
print(result.to_string())
print()

# Check arrival airports
print('=== Arrival airports ===')
result = con.execute('SELECT DISTINCT iata, airport_name FROM raw_arrivals ORDER BY iata').fetchdf()
print(result.to_string())
"

Something is off with the self-distance check. It says "nan out of 40 pairs" instead of "40 out of 40 pairs". This might be because the staging model uses `replace(b_name, ' ', '_')` on b_name but not on a_name. So when comparing `a_name = b_name`, the b_name has underscores while a_name has spaces. Let me verify.

The staging model's distance CTE has:
```sql
select
    a_name,
    replace(b_name, ' ', '_') as b_name,
    6371 * 2 * atan2(sqrt(area), sqrt(1-area) ) as distance_km
```

So `a_name` has spaces (e.g., "Bintulu Airport") while `b_name` has underscores (e.g., "Bintulu_Airport"). So `a_name = b_name` would never match in the staging model!

Wait, but self-distance should be computed for pairs where a."name" = b."name" (in the base_dist CTE). Let me check. In the `distance` CTE:

```sql
select
    a_name,
    replace(b_name, ' ', '_') as b_name,
    6371 * 2 * atan2(sqrt(area), sqrt(1-area) ) as distance_km
from base_area
```

The `a_name` and `b_name` here come from `base_dist`, where:
```sql
a."name" as a_name,
b."name" as b_name,
```

So both a_name and b_name are raw names with spaces. Then in the distance CTE, only b_name gets `replace(b_name, ' ', '_')`. So the comparison `a_name = b_name` won't work for self-pairs.

But in the core distance model (PIVOT), the columns are named after the replaced b_name values (with underscores), while a_name keeps spaces. This is the intended behavior.

The symmetry check passed (0 asymmetric pairs), so the distance matrix is symmetric. Good.
